caption:
Narrated Abu Musa: that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Every eye commits adultery, and when the woman uses perfume and she passes by a gathering, then she is like this and that.'" Meaning an adulteress.

Jami` at-Tirmidhi 2786. Part 33 of 52 in our series on everything the Quran and the Prophet's hadith say about zina. Swipe for the Arabic, English, Mandarin, Korean, Japanese, Malay, Thai and Spanish.

Sources on the final slide.

#Hadith #Chastity #IslamicReminder #Deen #Guidance

sourcing.primary_text: Jami` at-Tirmidhi 2786 (hadith-api numbering; Book 43, Hadith 58). Selected from a full-text scan of all hadith-api English editions (Bukhari, Muslim, Abu Dawud, Tirmidhi, Nasa'i, Ibn Majah, Malik, Nawawi, Dehlawi) for zina / adultery / fornication / illegal sexual intercourse / prostitution; one representative narration per distinct statement of the Prophet.
sourcing.arabic_and_english: Live-fetched twice on 2026-10-17 from cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/fawazahmed0/hadith-api@1/editions/ara-tirmidhi and eng-tirmidhi, HTTP 200, the two fetches diffed identical. Slides written programmatically from the API text.
sourcing.arabic_extraction: Arabic slide shows the Prophet's words only (text between the quotation marks, or a marked sub-range where the API Arabic has no quotes); chain of narrators omitted from the slide, not altered. Invisible directional marks and stray quote characters removed.
sourcing.english_note: English trimmed only at the edges where noted (chain/narrator commentary), punctuation restored at the end only. Final slide text: Narrated Abu Musa: that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Every eye commits adultery, and when the woman uses perfume and she passes by a gathering, then she is like this and that.'" Meaning an adulteress.
sourcing.grade: Grade per hadith-api: Hasan (Ahmad Muhammad Shakir); Hasan (Al-Albani); Hasan Sahih (Bashar Awad Maarouf); Isnaad Hasan (Zubair Ali Zai)
sourcing.chinese_korean_japanese_malay_thai_spani: hadith-api has no Chinese, Korean, Japanese, Malay, Thai or Spanish edition. These six slides are Claude's own translation from the verified Arabic and English, labelled on-slide as such; no scholar is named.
